_comment: Locations. id is added to LOCATION_ID_BASE and never reused (retired: 4). requires lists the event or item names the spot itself needs once you're in the room, kept apart from what reaching the room needs (so entrance rando can change one without the other); written even when the region implies it. category marks a location a yaml option can leave out (quest, crystal_berry, discovery, shop, item_shop). source says how the game marks it done: flag is the global flag the client watches, event the EventControl event that sets it, npc the character who gives it. source.give is the |giveitem,type,item,...| that hands out the vanilla item on that map (type -1 berries, 0 item, 1 key item, 2 medal): the client keeps it out of the inventory and shows the seed's item instead. source.pickup is an item lying in the world or buried in a dig spot (map, type: 0 item, 1 key item, 2 medal, 3 crystal berry, and item); its flag is the pickup's own activationflag. A story pickup (pickup.story) has no activationflag: it is known by the story event it starts (source.event) and checked by the flag that event sets. Instead of a flag: source.var and source.at_least (done when flagvar[var] reaches at_least; slot_data location_vars), source.berry (a crystal berry's crystalbflags index; location_berries), source.regional (a respawning pickup's regional flag), source.discovery (a journal discovery), source.shop and source.medal (a medal shop's badgeshops index and the medal; one location per copy it ever stocks), source.item_shop (an item shop's map, keeper and item; its first purchase is the check). Artifacts are events (no id): the game counts 7 artifact flags, and the goal is having enough of them. story_events are logic-only events (no id): a story step, placed in the region where it happens, whose item other rules require. The lists after them go to the client in slot_data, each entry a (map, entity): kept_open, story blockers kept out of the way so an area with locations never closes; kept_present, entities the story only makes later, made to exist from the start; scenery_hidden and scenery_present, flag-switched scenery hidden or shown from the start; present_from, an entity made from flag instead of its own requirement; held_until, an entity kept away until flag, on top of its own requirements; dialogue_flags, one dialogue line's flag repointed from flag to to.

The inn portrait, a journal discovery, also only from chapter 2.
The door into Madeleine's house; she and her butler stay away, so none of her story starts early.
The town's quest board, made from chapter 2; each quest's own requirements are checked before the logic counts on it.

The bounce mushroom back up to the pitfall room, so the trapdoor is never a dead end.
The door at the top of the bounce mushroom.
